candidates.title: bottom
candidates.text:
## st.bottom

`st.bottom` is a layout container pinned to the bottom of the main app area. Use it for chat inputs, toolbars, footers, and other controls that should stay visible while users scroll through your app content.

Elements can be passed to `st.bottom` using object notation and `with` notation.

The following two snippets are equivalent:

```python
# Object notation
st.bottom.[element_name]
```

```python
# "with" notation
with st.bottom:
    st.[element_name]
```

<Important>

`st.bottom` is only available in the **main app area**. Using it inside [`st.sidebar`](/develop/api-reference/layout/st.sidebar), [`st.dialog`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.dialog), or event containers (such as [`st.toast`](/develop/api-reference/status/st.toast)) raises an error.

</Important>

candidates.title: bottom
candidates.text:
## Add a sticky footer

Use `st.bottom` for footers, toolbars, or status bars that should remain visible at the bottom of the viewport:

```python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Dashboard")
st.line_chart({"sales": [10, 20, 15, 30, 25]})

with st.bottom:
    st.caption("© 2026 My Company · All rights reserved")
```

candidates.title: Widgets in an st.popover opened inside an st.dialog are occluded by the dialog and unusable
candidates.text:
### Summary

When an `st.popover` is used inside an `st.dialog`, the popover opens but its body
is rendered underneath the dialog's interaction layer. Widgets inside the popover
(e.g. a `selectbox`) cannot be interacted with, and clicking them lands on the
dialog's dismissable overlay — which can close the dialog. This is a regression
from the migration of `st.dialog` to React Aria (#15327); it worked in 1.58.0.

candidates.text:

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Unknown.

candidates.title: Hierarchical multipage navigation
candidates.text:
### Solution

**MVP:** A menu component with ability to have a tree-like structure with at least 1 level into it. Simple clicking (not radio). Ideally should be able to place it anywhere, like with any normal component (sidebar or main area, or column in main area - with embedded columns in roadmap this could give quite nice formatting options too).

**Possible additions:** I'm interested only in vertical menu, but a top-level menu could be nice, especially if it could be placed at the very top of the page (like sidebar, but top-bar).

**Preferred solution:** -

context.text:
## st.bottom

`st.bottom` is a layout container pinned to the bottom of the main app area. Use it for chat inputs, toolbars, footers, and other controls that should stay visible while users scroll through your app content.

Elements can be passed to `st.bottom` using object notation and `with` notation.

The following two snippets are equivalent:

```python
# Object notation
st.bottom.[element_name]
```

```python
# "with" notation
with st.bottom:
    st.[element_name]
```

<Important>

`st.bottom` is only available in the **main app area**. Using it inside [`st.sidebar`](/develop/api-reference/layout/st.sidebar), [`st.dialog`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.dialog), or event containers (such as [`st.toast`](/develop/api-reference/status/st.toast)) raises an error.

</Important>

context.title: bottom
context.text:
## Add a sticky footer

Use `st.bottom` for footers, toolbars, or status bars that should remain visible at the bottom of the viewport:

```python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Dashboard")
st.line_chart({"sales": [10, 20, 15, 30, 25]})

with st.bottom:
    st.caption("© 2026 My Company · All rights reserved")
```

context.text:
### Solution

**MVP:** A menu component with ability to have a tree-like structure with at least 1 level into it. Simple clicking (not radio). Ideally should be able to place it anywhere, like with any normal component (sidebar or main area, or column in main area - with embedded columns in roadmap this could give quite nice formatting options too).

**Possible additions:** I'm interested only in vertical menu, but a top-level menu could be nice, especially if it could be placed at the very top of the page (like sidebar, but top-bar).
